findings.title: Role-mapping checks drop manage-clients and master admins
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission. They never short-circuit on root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS), unlike canManage(ClientModel). hasPermission then returns false immediately when the caller is not in the same realm. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 installs MgmtPermissionsV2 for every realm, so this replaces the V1 evaluator: realm admins with manage-clients, and master-realm admins, can no longer map client roles, add composites, or map client-scope roles unless a fine-grained permission also grants it. V1 kept that role check inside its permission helper before any same-realm test. The new tests only use myadmin with no admin role, so they do not catch the regression. map-roles-client-scope has no test at all.

findings.title: Null all-clients resource NPEs permission checks
findings.body: If no per-client resource exists, hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) loads the type resource with getResourceTypeResource and immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource returns null when the Clients resource was never created, was deleted, or the schema is not supported for that server (admin permissions disabled while the admin-permissions client pointer remains). findByResource dereferences the resource, so the call throws NullPointerException. The no-argument hasPermission null-checks its lookup; this overload does not. View, manage, configure, and map-roles checks that reach this fallback then 500 instead of denying, for any caller who did not already pass an admin-role short-circuit.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never get the Clients schema
findings.body: init returns as soon as realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null, and nothing in this change syncs an already created resource server. The Clients resource and the new scopes configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite are only inserted when that client is first created. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions for Users keep the old server: the Clients resource is missing and getScope fails with "Scope [configure] does not exist" (and the same for the other new scope names) when a client permission is created. Evaluation then falls through to a null type resource and can 500. Only freshly initialized realms work.

findings.title: Client deletion throws when both FGAP features are enabled
findings.body: The removal listener is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, even if the V1 feature is also on. ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled always throws UnsupportedOperationException. With both features enabled, ClientRemovedEvent calls that method and the exception propagates from the provider listener, failing or rolling back client deletion. Role and group removal still use the V1 evaluators, so only clients are broken. The listener must not call the V2 implementation, or setPermissionsEnabled must be a no-op under V2.

findings.title: Runtime client permission methods throw instead of deciding
findings.body: Turning on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 makes ClientPermissionsV2 the client evaluator for every realm, not only realms that opted into admin permissions. canExchangeTo, isPermissionsEnabled, and getPermissions unconditionally throw UnsupportedOperationException. canExchangeTo is the token-exchange authorization check (authorized client plus subject token) and used to return a boolean, including role-based allow or deny; a throw is a 500, not a deny. isPermissionsEnabled and getPermissions are still the client management-permissions API and are reachable from any parent method that was not overridden, so those calls 500 as well. Unimplemented V2 behavior needs to fail closed or keep the manage-clients role path, not throw. getEvaluationContext in this class is unused, so the exchange path was left unfinished.

findings.title: Per-client resources are stored with no type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource now resolves Clients, then resourceStore.create plus updateScopes, but never setType(resourceType). The all-clients resource created in init does set type to Clients. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission discovers candidates only via findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Individual grants therefore create resources that name lookup can see (hasPermission uses findByName) but the type query cannot. Any admin listing or filter that uses getClientsWithPermission omits every specifically permitted client, while a direct check of that same client can still succeed.

findings.title: All-clients permission is returned as the id Clients
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every Clients-typed resource whose evaluation grants the scope. The schema resource created for "all clients" is named Clients and has that type, so a type-level grant puts the literal string Clients into the set. That is not a client UUID. Callers that keep clients where granted.contains(client.getId()) will not treat the grant as access to every client, and nothing expands the type resource into real client ids. There is no global canMapRoles() to compensate, so an all-clients map-roles or view permission does not show those clients in filters that rely on this method.

findings.title: Client resources are returned with a null display name
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases Users: the type resource becomes "All users" and other names are resolved to usernames, throwing ModelIllegalStateException if the user is gone. Client resources are stored under the internal client id (resolveClient returns client.getId()) and are created without a display name, so they hit return resource.getDisplayName() and come back null. The all-clients resource is named Clients and is not labeled "All clients". Permission listings for the new type show blank names, and a deleted client does not surface the missing-object error used for users.

findings.title: V2 client grants are not removed when the client is deleted
findings.body: Per-client FGAP resources are named with the client id and are not foreign-keyed to the client, so deleting the client does not cascade them. The only hook added here is the ClientRemovedEvent listener, and the new feature gate skips that hook unless ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. In the V2-only setup this work targets, client deletion leaves the admin-permissions resource and its scope permissions in place. Listings keep a grant for a client that no longer exists, and getResourceName returns null for it. setPermissionsEnabled cannot be used to clean this up because the V2 implementation throws.

findings.title: Client tests rotate myclient's secret and do not restore it
findings.body: testConfigureOnlyOneClient calls generateNewSecret and invalidateRotatedSecret on myclient and never puts the original secret back. realmAdminClient is injected for the class as client myclient; the sibling impersonation helper logs in with client secret mysecret. After rotation, refresh for that confidential client fails, so later methods in this class can 401 once the access token is no longer reused. testManageOnlyOneClient also renames myclient and removeDefaultClientScope without restoring either, and AfterEach only deletes scope permissions, so later methods share that leaked client state.

findings.title: requireView javadoc says a void method returns true
findings.body: The new javadoc on requireView says it returns true if canView() returns true, but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException when the check fails, same as requireManage. requireViewClientScopes (line 102) has the same error: it says it returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true. Implementors reading only the contract will treat these as predicates instead of enforcing checks.
